questions.q: Why are versioning and encryption configured as separate resources attached to `aws_s3_bucket`, rather than inline attributes?
options: Because S3 buckets cannot support versioning or encryption at all
Because that matches how the AWS provider's resource types for these settings are structured
Because inline attributes are deprecated in every AWS resource
Because versioning requires a separate AWS account
questions.explain: The aws provider models S3 bucket versioning and server-side encryption as their own resource types, each referencing the bucket's id, rather than as attributes inside the bucket block itself.

questions.q: What problem does enabling versioning on the product-images bucket solve?
options: It makes uploads faster
It lets an accidentally overwritten or deleted object be recovered from an earlier version
It automatically resizes images
It removes the need for IAM permissions
questions.explain: Versioning keeps prior versions of an object, so an accidental overwrite or delete doesn't permanently lose the original.

questions.explain: The assume_role_policy specifies who, or what service, is trusted to assume the role — in this lesson, the Lambda service itself.

questions.q: What does 'least privilege' mean in the context of the IAM policy attached to the order-confirmation role?
options: Granting the broadest permissions available, to avoid future changes
Granting only the specific actions the role actually needs, such as reading one bucket and sending email, and nothing more
Granting no permissions at all
Granting permissions only to human users, never to services
questions.explain: Least privilege means scoping a role's policy to exactly the actions it needs to do its job — here, reading product images and sending email — so a bug or compromise can't do unrelated damage.

questions.q: In the `aws_lambda_function` block, what does the `role` attribute do?
options: Stores the function's long-lived AWS access key
References the IAM role the function assumes at runtime, instead of the function holding its own credentials
Sets the function's memory allocation
Specifies which S3 bucket triggers the function
questions.explain: role points to the IAM role resource, which Lambda assumes every time the function runs — the pattern AWS favors over functions or services holding their own long-lived credentials.
